assessment.headline: DAY 31. Sensex crashes to 71,948. Brent $115. Rupee 94.84 ATL. But 8 Indian carriers crossed. FY26 ends in crisis.
assessment.body:
FY26 ended the way no one imagined — Sensex at 71,948 after crashing 1,636 points. Nifty at 22,331. This is the worst monthly market performance in 6 years. Brent has surged past $115 — up 55% in one month. The rupee hit a new all-time low of 94.84. FII outflow reached $12.3 billion in March — an all-time record.

But India's quiet operation is working: 8 carriers have now safely crossed Hormuz — Shivalik, Nanda Devi, Jag Laadki (crude), Pine Gas, Jag Vasant, 2 SCI carriers, and now BW Elm + BW Tyr (94,000 MT LPG with Navy escort). BW Tyr reaches Mumbai March 31. 18 ships + 485 crew still remain. 942+ seafarers have been repatriated.

The dual chokepoint threat is the gravest development: Houthis fired 2 salvos at Israel and could block Bab al-Mandeb. If both Hormuz AND Red Sea close, India's entire maritime energy supply is severed — no Cape of Good Hope reroute helps.

Verified India numbers:
• 28 ships at peak → 18 remain + 485 seafarers
• 8 carriers crossed safely (carrying ~450,000+ MT of LPG/crude)
• Op Urja Suraksha: 5+ Navy warships escorting
• Still waiting: Jag Vikram, Green Asha, Green Sanvi
• Excise cut ₹10/L. RBI burned $15B. Forex -$19B
• 91% LPG from Gulf. Indian basket $125/bbl. Dubai physical $126
• FII $12.3B outflow. ₹44L+ Cr destroyed. PhonePe halted IPO

April 6 deadline = 7 days. Pentagon is planning ground raids on Kharg Island. 4-way Islamabad talks underway. The WEF called this a 'structural shock to the world economy.' The IEA called it 'the greatest energy security challenge in history.' India is simultaneously getting some LPG through — and facing the worst economic month since the 2008 crisis.
